The gray region is exactly the part inside the square but not belonging to these four triangles. Then reason: The problem gives that the side length of each equilateral triangle is 2. The height of an equilateral triangle with side length 2 is (\sqrt{3}/2)\cdot 2=\sqrt{3}. Since the base of each triangle is on a side of the square, and the vertex is at the center of the square, the distance from the center of the square to any side is \sqrt{3}, and the side length of the square is 2\sqrt{3}. Therefore the area of the square is (2\sqrt{3})^2=12. The area of each equilateral triangle is (\sqrt{3}/4)\cdot 2^2=\sqrt{3}, and the total area of the four triangles is 4\sqrt{3}. Shaded area = area of square - area of four triangles = 12-4\sqrt{3}.

claims.source: Therefore the area of the square is (2\sqrt{3})^2=12

claims.claim: The area of each equilateral triangle is \sqrt{3}.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The area of each equilateral triangle is (\sqrt{3}/4)\cdot 2^2=\sqrt{3}

claims.claim: The total area of the four triangles is 4\sqrt{3}.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The total area of the four triangles is 4\sqrt{3}

claims.claim: The shaded area equals the area of the square minus the area of the four triangles.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Shaded area = square area - areas of four triangles

claims.claim: The shaded area is 12-4\sqrt{3}.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Shaded area = square area - areas of four triangles = 12-4\sqrt{3}
